name: Comfort Wear
palette: white / soft lavender backgrounds, Comfort Wear purple (#7A2FE0) for headlines and pills, black body text
font_style: bold geometric sans-serif headlines (like Poppins/Montserrat ExtraBold), clean sans body text
prompt_rules: The shoe MUST be the exact shoe in the attached studio reference photo, unchanged: same colors, stretch-knit sock-style upper with pull tab, grid-of-small-squares pattern on the side panel, elastic bungee laces with a round toggle, double-chevron logo on the inner collar, chunky rocker midsole with a wavy side profile, lug outsole. Keep its proportions and every detail; only change its angle, lighting and setting as the layout requires. Do not invent a different shoe, logo or sole.
This is a women's shoe: the person wearing it is always a woman (women's proportions and styling). Men may appear only as gift-givers or in the background, never wearing the shoe.
Render every word of on-image text exactly as written in quotes, spelled correctly, and no other text.

Add nothing the description doesn't ask for: no extra feature lists, icon callouts, price tags, badges, panels or captions. Never show other brands' logos or products; competitors appear as text names only.
High-end e-commerce photography quality, sharp focus, natural soft shadows, no watermarks, no extra logos.
claims_to_avoid: money-back guarantee, free/easy returns or fast shipping (top complaints in reviews and the survey)
'orthopedic approved', 'podiatrist recommended', 'doctor recommended' or any cure/treatment claim
specific review counts or star ratings unless confirmed

black_white.label: black with white accents (team name: BlackWhite)

navy_blue.label: navy with bright blue accents (team name: WhiteBlue/BlueWhite)

nurse.name: Hospital nurse on 12-hour shifts
nurse.source: Biggest historical winners; 12% of survey jobs; PF 27%, 'just comfort' 26%

cna_caregiver.name: CNA / home health aide / caregiver
cna_caregiver.source: Survey n=380; 30% 'no pain, just comfort'; long shifts, lifting, low pay so price matters

restaurant.name: Server, line cook, bartender (doubles, wet floors)
restaurant.source: Survey n=1,055, mostly under 50; r/Serverlife: 'cheap shoes kill your ankles, knees & back', Hoka Bondi SR too pricey

retail_warehouse.name: Cashier, retail, warehouse/factory on concrete
retail_warehouse.source: Survey n=1,377; PF 27–33%; databank 'cashiers on concrete'

housekeeping.name: Housekeeping, cleaning, janitorial
housekeeping.source: Survey n=375; highest PF share (35%); strong overlap with Spanish-speaking workers

teacher.name: Teacher / paraprofessional
teacher.source: Survey n=775, 29% PF; forums: 'comfortable or cute, hardly ever both'

stylist.name: Hairstylist / salon / beauty
stylist.source: Survey n=152; 'on my feet all day'; style-conscious

active_retiree.name: Active retiree, 65+ (walks, grandkids, errands)
active_retiree.source: Survey: largest job group (27%), 47% aged 65+; 24% 'just comfort', neuropathy 14%

steady_feet.name: Older adult worried about balance, swelling or neuropathy
steady_feet.source: Survey neuropathy 10%; Mayo Clinic Connect: slip-ons that 'accommodate daily foot swelling', grip soles, side support

traveler.name: Traveler (Disney, Europe, cruises, 20k-step days)
traveler.source: Kyro 293/369 travel videos ($58k, 2.15 ROAS); team statics 'Paris/Barcelona 50 steps'

walker_weightloss.name: New walker / weight-loss journey (incl. GLP-1)
walker_weightloss.source: Winner 'I lost 50lbs+ after walking 20,000 steps' ($93k); team GLP-1 statics; rapid weight loss thins the foot's fat pad

comfort_only.name: No diagnosis, just wants comfortable everyday shoes
comfort_only.source: Survey: 22% 'No foot pain, only need for comfort'; 71% shop for 'comfort'

gift_for_her.name: Gift buyer for mom, grandma or wife
gift_for_her.source: Own knowledge: comfort-shoe gifting (Mother's/Father's Day, holidays); parents 65+ are the core wearer

language_rules.es: All on-image text is in Spanish exactly as written in quotes, as a Spanish-speaking person living in the USA would say it (neutral US Latino, Mexican-leaning, using 'tú'). Keep every accent and sign: á é í ó ú ñ ¿ ¡. Numbers in US format (12,000 not 12.000; $59.95). Do not translate brand names. Use only the Spanish text given in quotes: do not add feature lists, icons with captions, price tags, badges or extra panels.

audience: Women only: the product is a women's shoe. Whoever wears the shoe in an ad is always a woman; men may appear only as gift-givers or background people, never wearing the product.
